item.title: Quditology: harnessing many levels for quantum information processing
item.description:
Pay dirt review — Survey of qudit quantum information hardware demonstrates that multi-level d>2 architectures match the Hilbert space of 70 qubits using 24 qudits with d=8, achieving gate-depth reductions exceeding one order of magnitude in dedicated quantum simulations.

Grade 0.499 · 2.6σ above the day's baseline · matched “Quantum information with Rydberg atoms” · Abhijit Chakraborty, Zheng Shi, Noah Goss, Irfan Siddiqi, Barry C. Sanders, Christine A. Muschik

Figure

Landscape of qudit implementations showing controllable qudit dimension d on the horizontal axis versus the number of interacting qudits n on the vertical axis across experimental platforms.

Asks

What is the current experimental state of the art in high-fidelity state preparation, control, measurement, and fault tolerance across diverse qudit platforms?

But

Increased spectral crowding, heightened sensitivity to phase decoherence, energy relaxation across higher levels, and elevated classical and quantum crosstalk.

Tools

trapped ions · superconducting circuits · solid-state nuclear spins · photonic circuits · neutral atoms

Abstract

Quantum computing offers the prospect of surpassing classical computation on certain tasks by leveraging quantum coherence and entanglement. However, a significant gap remains between current quantum hardware and the requirements to transcend what classical computers can achieve, with decoherence limiting the capacity of storing quantum information and the number of logical steps that can be executed reliably. In the long term, fault tolerance bridges this gap, but simply changing the numerical base from binary to higher base d is a viable way to 'squeeze more juice'---get more quantum information processing---from a quantum computer of given size. Additionally, for quantum simulations, qudits offer a natural encoding scheme for high-dimensional physical degrees of freedom. Here, we review recent experimental progress in high-fidelity preparation, control, and measurement of qudits across various platforms such as trapped ions, superconducting circuits, solid-state nuclear spins, photonic systems, and neutral atoms. We highlight early demonstrations of qudit-based quantum simulation, computation and error suppression enabled by these developments, heralding the transition of qudits from conceptual constructs to viable building blocks for quantum technologies. Finally, we outline key challenges and potential future directions for scalable qudit quantum information processing.

item.title: Complementary mechanisms of critical quantum metrology
item.description:
Pay dirt theory — Critical estimation of intrinsic parameter φ achieves δφ∼N−2/3 solely through suppressed quantum noise without enhanced response. This matches the δr∼N−2/3 scaling of parameter r, which is driven by diverging susceptibility despite increased noise.

Grade 0.447 · 2.0σ above the day's baseline · matched “Quantum information with Rydberg atoms” · Nikita Leppenen, Shaked Levy, Ephraim Shahmoon

Figure

Plots (a)-(d) show estimation errors, N−2/3 finite-size scaling, noise/signal decompositions, and the N2/3 energy gap opening versus spin number N for the Ising ground state.

Asks

Can quantum noise suppression at criticality enhance the estimation of intrinsic system parameters without relying on enhanced susceptibility or external interferometric encoding?

Before

Standard quantum limit error scales as N−1/2; previous critical metrology achieved super-SQL scaling exclusively via enhanced susceptibility of order parameters.

But

Asymptotic to large spin counts N≫1; restricted to finite-size critical boundary r=rN∼1−(3/N)2/3 before mean-field transition softens.

Tools

coherently radiating spin states (CRSS) · driven-dissipative Dicke master equation · all-to-all transverse-field Ising Hamiltonian · exact numerical diagonalization

Abstract

Critical metrology conventionally exploits enhanced susceptibility to a system parameter near a phase transition. Here we identify a complementary mechanism for critically enhanced estimation of intrinsic system parameters via suppressed quantum noise rather than enhanced response. We demonstrate both mechanisms in coherently radiating spin states (CRSS)-correlated states of N spin-1/2 particles defined as asymptotic eigenstates of the collective-spin lowering operator with complex eigenvalue r e^(-iφ). At the critical value r=1, CRSS exhibit a second-order transition. We show that near criticality, estimation of r benefits from enhanced susceptibility despite increased noise, whereas estimation of φ benefits from suppressed quantum noise without enhanced response. Remarkably, both yield the same estimation error ∼N^(-2/3), improving over the standard quantum limit N^(-1/2). For φ, this establishes quantum-enhanced metrology of phases intrinsic to the critical system, rather than phases externally encoded by interferometry. We demonstrate these results for CRSS realizations in both dissipative (superradiant) and Hamiltonian (Ising) systems relevant to cavity QED and trapped ions, where fast preparation of CRSS is shown possible thanks to gap opening. Applications to metrology of coupling rates and phases or optical lengths are discussed.

item.title: A bright source of high-dimensional spatially entangled photon pairs based on beam-like Type-II SPDC
item.description:
Worth a look new result — Beam-like Type-II SPDC yields at least 62-dimensional spatial entanglement in a d=121 basis with fidelity lower bound Fmin⁡=0.5052>B61=61/121, alongside ∼1.56-fold higher single-photon and ∼1.45-fold higher coincidence rates than collinear Type-I SPDC.

Grade 0.412 · 1.6σ above the day's baseline · matched “Quantum information with Rydberg atoms” · Ming Zhang, Zhiming Qing, Zhi-Cheng Ren, Jianping Ding, Xi-Lin Wang, Hui-Tian Wang

Figure

Spatial-mode grids and corresponding 121×121 correlation matrices across mutually unbiased momentum and position bases certifying high-dimensional spatial entanglement.

Asks

Can high detected brightness and high-dimensional spatial entanglement be realized simultaneously in a single SPDC photon-pair source?

Before

Collinear Type-I SPDC baseline under identical pumping and acquisition conditions gave lower count rates by factors of ∼1.56 (singles) and ∼1.45 (coincidences).

But

Broadened experimental correlation widths due to residual spatial walk-off, optical aberrations, and camera pixel pitch (16.38~μm). Discretized into uniform 11×11 macropixel grids with 32.76~μm intermode gaps.

Tools

beam-like Type-II SPDC · β-barium borate (BBO) crystal · SPAD512 array camera · two-basis entanglement certification (MUBs)

Abstract

Bright sources of high-dimensional spatially entangled photon pairs are increasingly required for the rapid advancement of quantum technologies. However, simultaneously achieving high brightness and high-dimensional spatial entanglement through spontaneous parametric down-conversion (SPDC) remains challenging. Here, we demonstrate a bright source of high-dimensional spatially entangled photon pairs using beam-like Type-II SPDC in a β-barium borate crystal. Compared with a conventional collinear Type-I source, it exhibits a ∼1.56-fold enhancement in the detected single-photon count rate and a ∼1.45-fold enhancement in the coincidence count rate. Measurements of position correlations and momentum anti-correlations certify at least 62-dimensional spatial entanglement within a 121-dimensional basis. These correlations are further exploited to demonstrate quantum imaging in both the position and momentum domains. These characteristics make the source a practical resource for high-dimensional photonic quantum technologies.

item.title: High-Dimensional Single-Photon Frequency Conversion for Orbital Angular Momentum Comb State
item.description:
Worth a look new result — Heralded single-photon orbital angular momentum comb state generated with dimension up to 128 at 1560 nm, achieving fidelity 0.787 and effective dimension Deff≃100.7. Sum-frequency conversion to 520 nm demonstrated for dimensions 4, 8, and 16 with fidelities 0.901, 0.881, and 0.804.

Grade 0.412 · 1.6σ above the day's baseline · matched “Quantum information with Rydberg atoms” · Sheng-Qiang Jia, Hao Sheng, Zhiming Qing, Li Fan, Jianping Ding, Jia-Min Xu, Zhi-Cheng Ren, Xi-Lin Wang, Hui-Tian Wang

Figure

Measured versus target modal intensity distributions (upper panels) and relative phases (lower panels) as a function of OAM mode order for comb dimensions d=4,8,16,32, and 128 at 1560 nm.

Asks

How can high-dimensional single-photon orbital angular momentum comb states be scalably generated and coherently frequency-converted between communication and visible bands?

Before

OAM states spanning tens of modes were previously experimentally prepared and characterized.

But

Frequency conversion tested up to dimension 16 only; low conversion efficiency makes d2 projections for d>16 take over two weeks.

Tools

PPKTP spontaneous parametric down-conversion · type-0 sum-frequency generation · custom liquid-crystal phase plate · spatial light modulator (SLM) · quantum state tomography

Abstract

The orbital angular momentum (OAM) degree of freedom provides an important resource for constructing high-dimensional optical quantum information systems. However, the generation of high-dimensional single-photon OAM comb state and its high-fidelity frequency conversion remain challenging due to limited spatial modulation resolution, imperfect mode matching, and finite nonlinear conversion efficiency. Here, we proposed and experimentally demonstrated a scalable scheme for the generation and frequency conversion of high-dimensional single-photon OAM comb state. We prepared a single-photon OAM comb state with a dimension of up to 128, achieving a fidelity of 0.787 between the reconstructed and target states and an effective dimension of 100. Furthermore, using the sum-frequency generation, we demonstrated the frequency upconversion of single-photon high-dimensional OAM comb state from the communication band to a visible wavelength of 520 nm, while verifying the preservation of both the OAM mode distribution and phase information through density matrix reconstruction. Our work established a versatile platform for the generation, manipulation, and characterization of high-dimensional OAM comb states, with potential applications in cross-band quantum information transfer, high-capacity quantum communication, and high-dimensional quantum networks.

item.title: On-Demand Tailoring of High-Dimensional Orbital Angular Momentum States via a Phase-Only Hologram
item.description:
Worth a look new method — Iterative phase-only modulation tailors high-dimensional OAM state amplitude and phase with twofold generation-efficiency enhancement for N≥10. Reconstructed fidelity reaches 98.4% at dimension 4, 92.0% at 50, and 82.0% at 128.

Grade 0.410 · 1.6σ above the day's baseline · matched “Quantum information with Rydberg atoms” · Hao Sheng, Zi-Shuo Wang, Sheng-Qiang Jia, Zi-Mo Cheng, Li Fan, Jianping Ding, Jia-Min Xu, Zhi-Cheng Ren, Xi-Lin Wang, Hui-Tian Wang

Figure

Generation efficiency as a function of OAM dimension N up to 100 for equal-amplitude zero-phase superposition states, comparing this method against blazed grating modulation and multiple-pixel encoding.

Asks

Can both amplitude and phase of high-dimensional orbital angular momentum states be tailored on demand using a single phase-only hologram without extra modulation degrees?

Before

Blazed grating modulation and multiple-pixel encoding; method achieves a twofold efficiency enhancement over both for N≥10.

But

Pure phase modulation leaving unmodulated power in non-target OAM modes; total measured 4D efficiency was 39.0% due to an approximately 80.0% overall coupling efficiency.

Tools

iterative pure spiral phase algorithm · spatial light modulators · quantum state tomography · maximum-likelihood estimation · single-mode fiber coupling

Abstract

Photonic orbital angular momentum (OAM) provides a naturally discrete and unbounded Hilbert space for high-dimensional encoding and has emerged as a powerful degree of freedom for advanced information processing. On-demand tailoring of both the amplitude and phase profiles of high-dimensional OAM states is essential for numerous applications, particularly in quantum information science. Here, we propose and experimentally demonstrate an efficient method for achieving such on-demand tailoring using a purely phase-only modulation scheme. The measured fidelity remains above 80% even for a 128-dimensional state, demonstrating the scalability of the approach. Compared with previous techniques, our method achieves significantly higher generation efficiency, and this advantage becomes more pronounced as the dimensionality increases. Moreover, our approach substantially reduces experimental complexity while maintaining precise control, thereby offering a practical and scalable solution for high-dimensional OAM state engineering in both classical and quantum information processing.

item.title: Exact monogamy of steering and remote Wigner negativity for multimode Gaussian nodes
item.description:
Worth a look theory — A Gaussian node with k modes can be steered with Gaussian measurements by at most 2k−1 single-mode neighbors, matching the exact maximum number of neighbors made Wigner-negative by a single heralded operation.

Grade 0.404 · 1.6σ above the day's baseline · matched “Cavity-based quantum networks with single atoms and optical photons” · Sudip Chakrabarty

Figure

Network schematic showing a k-mode Gaussian node coupled via an arbitrary Gaussian channel to multiple single-mode neighbors.

Asks

How many neighbors can steer a multimode Gaussian node of k modes, and how many neighbors can one non-Gaussian heralded event at the node make Wigner-negative?

But

Global states must be Gaussian. Counts beyond two measurement settings are certified numerically up to k=50 rather than proven analytically for all k.

Tools

covariance matrix share bound · harmonic tight frames · Schur complements · semidefinite programming certified steering inequalities

Abstract

Optical quantum networks route correlations through nodes that hold several modes and are linked to many neighbors. Steering is the correlation behind one-sided device-independent tasks and behind the remote preparation of non-Gaussian states. It is monogamous for a single mode, which can be steered by only one party, but how many neighbors can steer a node with k modes was not known. We show that for Gaussian states the answer is exactly 2k-1 when the neighbors use Gaussian measurements, with any number of measurement settings. The limit follows from a simple bound. To every neighbor we assign a share, computed from the covariance matrix, and we prove that the shares of all neighbors add up to at most k, irrespective of the amount of squeezing, amplification or noise the network contains. A neighbor steers the node by Gaussian measurements exactly when its share exceeds one half, and a network built from a harmonic tight frame reaches the limit. The same number governs remote Wigner negativity. A heralded non-Gaussian operation at the node can make at most 2k-1 neighbors Wigner negative, and in our network a single heralded projection makes all of them negative in the same run. With n settings of arbitrary measurements, at most nk-1 neighbors can steer the node or violate a Bell inequality with it. More than 2k-1 neighbors can therefore steer the node or violate a Bell inequality with it only if they use non-Gaussian measurements with at least three settings, whereas entanglement can reach any number of neighbors. These results determine exactly how many neighbors one multimode node can serve with steering and with remote Wigner negativity.

item.title: A scalable dense silicon qubit architecture with logical operations
item.description:
Worth a look new method — Proposed dense silicon spin architecture needs code distance of at least 21 to reach logical error rates below 10−10 per syndrome cycle, integrating over 120,000 logical qubits on 100 mm × 100 mm chip.

Grade 0.404 · 1.5σ above the day's baseline · matched “trapped-ion gates, shuttling and QCCD architectures” · Masahiro Tadokoro, Tetsuo Kodera

Asks

How to design a scalable dense silicon spin qubit architecture that integrates error correction, qubit transport, wiring constraints, and transversal logical gates?

But

Theoretical design and numerical estimation based on experimentally demonstrated parameters; assumes optimized wiring efficiency.

Tools

rotated surface code · 1D spin shuttling data lanes · cross junctions for transversal CNOT · CMOS-compatible multiplexed control analysis

Abstract

Fault-tolerant quantum computing (FTQC) requires a large number of physical qubits to encode logical qubits with sufficiently low error rates. Silicon spin qubits are a promising platform because of their small footprint, compatibility with semiconductor manufacturing technologies, and demonstrated high-fidelity operations. However, realizing a scalable architecture that supports quantum error correction, qubit transport, wiring, and logical gate operations remains a major challenge. Here, we propose a scalable dense silicon spin qubit architecture designed to support large-scale FTQC. The architecture consists of qubit memories, data qubit lanes, and cross junctions. Qubit memories store logical qubits encoded using the rotated surface code and support logical single-qubit operations. Data qubit lanes enable high-speed one-dimensional spin shuttling for connectivity between logical qubits, while cross junctions provide routing functionality and implement transversal logical CNOT gates. Using experimentally demonstrated silicon spin qubit parameters, we evaluate logical error rates as a function of code distance and estimate that a code distance of at least 21 is required to achieve logical error rates below 10⁻¹⁰ per syndrome cycle. We further analyze wiring constraints based on CMOS-compatible multiplexed control schemes and show that, with optimized wiring efficiency, more than 120,000 logical qubits could be integrated on a 100 mm × 100 mm chip. These results provide a practical roadmap toward large-scale FTQC based on silicon spin qubit technology.
